title: Fixed coastline, inland ice
description: The sea level equation is solved with a fixed ocean geometry. The ice cap sits inland and never reaches the ocean basin, so the only coupling is through the uniform water layer and the deformation and geoid it produces.

source.citation: Martinec, Z. et al. (2018). Geophysical Journal International 215(1), 389-414.

$outputs_comment: U is surface vertical displacement, N is geoid displacement, S is sea-surface variation, all along meridional cross-sections at the terminal time. h_UF is the thickness of the uniform water layer, ice_mass_grounded and ice_mass_floating are ice masses, and ocean_area is the ocean area as a fraction of 4 pi, all as functions of time. The list holds what the paper compares for this case.

comparison.$comment: Source: Martinec et al. (2018), section 5, figures 3 to 19. Difference intervals apply to the profiles at the terminal time. See docs/protocol/martinec2018.qmd, section Comparison method.

reference_data.reference: VEGA, in resultsB_2026/Z_ZM_load.out and Z_ZM_basin.out. The basin profile has 359 rows and is a coarse copy; see correction martinec2018-caseD-vega-profile-grid.
reference_data.published_figure: Figures 5 and 6, with figure 4 showing the ice and basin geometry
